title: Eval Harness + Prompt Set Onboarding, Model Onboarding & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Sofia Nguyen
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook describes the standardized process for: (1) onboarding prompt sets into the eval harness, (2) model onboarding for serving, (3) applying quantization profiles, and (4) an operational regression triage flow. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, Model Onboarding owners, SREs that run the eval harness, and Product owners who define quality guardrails.

Summary of objectives
- Ensure repeatable, reviewable prompt-set onboarding with metadata and versioning.
- Provide deterministic eval harness runs with traceable config and performance baselines.
- Define quantization profiles and risk buckets for safe deployment.
- Provide a clear, SLA-driven regression triage playbook for eval regressions and production quality alerts.

Who should follow this playbook
- Applied ML Engineers (owners of eval definitions and prompt sets)
- Model Onboarding engineers (owners of model packaging and performance validation)
- SRE / Infra (owners of harness CI and compute pools)
- Product / QA (owners of pass/fail criteria and user-facing quality)

Key definitions and services
- Eval Harness (service: eval-harness-service): central test runner for prompt-set evaluations, runs locally or in CI, produces artifact bundle in S3: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{run_id}/
- Prompt-set (artifact): JSONL file with metadata and canonical prompts (metadata fields defined below)
- Runbook ID: EV-<YYYYMMDD>-<SEQUENCE> assigned to triage incidents
- Baseline: last accepted model+prompt-set evaluation artifacts used for regression comparisons

Onboarding checklist: Prompt sets
1. Create prompt-set artifact (JSONL) following schema: id, owner, description, domain, tags, inputs, expected_outputs (gold), difficulty, seed_examples.
2. Add metadata file prompt-set-{id}-meta.yaml with fields: annotation_instructions, sampling_policy, data_sources, privacy_flags. Example YAML snippet:

```yaml
id: ps-product-faq-2026-01
owner: @sofia.nguyen
description: Customer-facing product FAQ prompts used for release notes generation tests
domain: product_documentation
tags: [faq,generation,release-notes]
annotation_instructions: >
  Annotators should compare generated answer to gold using a 3-point scale: CORRECT/AMBIGUOUS/INCORRECT
sampling_policy: stratified across product areas, 50% short prompts
privacy_flags: none
```

3. Run local lint: `eval-harness-cli lint --prompt-set prompt-set-{id}.jsonl` (failure -> fix schema issues).
4. Run smoke eval: `eval-harness-cli run --prompt-set prompt-set-{id}.jsonl --profile smoke --output s3://redwood-evals/drafts/{id}/`
5. Submit PR to applied-ml repo: `applied-ml/prompt-sets/{id}` with metadata, sample outputs, and CI link. Include reviewer from list: model-onboarding, QA.
6. CI will run full harness (see CI config below) and publish results artifact; if CI checks pass (see pass criteria) the prompt-set is marked in the catalog as APPROVED.

Prompt-set metadata (required fields)
| field | format | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| id | string | short-dashed id, unique |
| owner | @username | primary owner for triage |
| domain | enumerated | e.g., product_documentation, search, summarization |
| tags | list | up to 8 tags |
| expected_outputs | list | gold answers for evaluation metrics |
| privacy_flags | enum | none | pii | restricted |

Eval harness configuration and CI
- CI job name: eval-harness/full-run/{prompt_set_id}/{model_version}
- Default compute: gpu-pool-eval (A100-40GB shared pool) or cpu-small for fast smoke runs.
- Timeout: 4 hours for full runs, 10 minutes for smoke runs.
- Artifact retention: 90 days in S3 (longer retention available by request).

Sample CI YAML snippet:
```yaml
jobs:
  eval_full_run:
    runs-on: self-hosted-eval
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Run eval harness
        run: |
          eval-harness-cli run --prompt-set prompt-set-{id}.jsonl --model {model_uri} --profile full --output s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{run_id}/
```

Pass/fail criteria (default)
- Primary metric pass: exact-match / BLEU / QA-F1 as defined per prompt-set. The metric and threshold must be documented in prompt-set metadata.
- Default thresholds:
  - QA-F1 >= 0.78 (for QA-type prompt sets)
  - Exact match >= 0.65 (for structured generation)
  - Average hallucination rate <= 2% (measured via heuristics and human checks)
- Regression detection: a drop in primary metric >= 2 percentage points relative to baseline triggers automated regression alert.

Model onboarding checklist (serving readiness)
1. Packaging and manifest: model manifest must include model_id, architecture, tokenizer, expected_seq_len, kv_cache_compat, quantization_profiles (see below).
2. Performance baseline: run benchmarking suite (tool: runtime-bench) across representative sequences; collect tokens/sec, p95 latency, and memory peaks. Expected report: s3://redwood-performance/{model_id}/benchmarks/{date}.
3. Quality baseline: run eval-harness full runs against approved prompt-sets (at minimum: product_faq, summarization_core, safety_sanity). Attach eval artifacts to model onboarding PR.
4. Safety checks: run safety scanners and filter tests (service: safety-gate). If any flagged content >0.5% fail rate, escalate to Applied ML lead and Safety team.
5. Quantization recommendation: attach suggested quantization_profile id and expected quality impact delta (estimated via calibration runs).
6. Deployment gating: model is eligible for staging when: regression alerts = none, perf within 10% of expected, and security scan = clean.

Quantization profiles and risk buckets
- Profiles are named: qp-{model_family}-{bits}-{mode} e.g., qp-gpt2-8bit-lora or qp-llama2-4bit-qAT.
- Each profile record must include: bits, algorithm (PTQ, QAT), expected memory reduction, expected throughput uplift, validation_delta (expected metric drop), tested_prompt_sets.

Example quantization profile table:
| profile_id | bits | algorithm | expected_token_throughput_change | expected_quality_delta | risk_bucket | recommended_deployment |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| qp-llama2-4bit-pdq | 4 | PDQ-PTQ | +1.8x | -0.8% | low | cpu-inference, on-prem |
| qp-mistral-8bit-qAT | 8 | QAT | +1.1x | -0.2% | minimal | hosted-api |
| qp-ggml-4bit-legacy | 4 | legacy-PTQ | +2.0x | -3.5% | high | internal-research-only |

Quantization validation steps
1. Run quantized model through eval-harness against the same prompt-set baseline.
2. Measure primary metric delta and hallucination heuristics.
3. If quality_delta > 2% or hallucination increase > 1.5pp, mark profile as HIGH RISK and require manual approval from Applied ML lead and Product QA.
4. Capture calibration artifacts in s3://redwood-quantization/{profile_id}/{run_id}/

Regression detection and triage playbook
- Monitoring: continuous evals run daily for critical prompt-sets and weekly for secondary sets. Monitoring system: eval-monitor (alerts -> PagerDuty team: applied-ml-regression).
- Alerting thresholds:
  - P0: primary metric drop >= 5pp or hallucination spike >= 3pp -> page on-call and create Runbook EV-INC/SEV1
  - P1: primary metric drop between 2-5pp -> create ticket, email owners, auto-run detailed diagnostics
  - P2: drop < 2pp -> log and schedule in weekly triage unless persistent for >3 consecutive runs

Immediate triage steps (within 1 hour for P0/P1)
1. Assign triage Runbook EV-<date>-<seq>.
2. Verify alert: reproduce failing eval in harness with full artifact set and `--debug` enabled.
3. Check for recent changes: model rollouts (router logs), quantization changes, prompt-set edits, infra changes (kernel updates).
4. If regression reproduces locally, compare diffs against baseline artifacts with `eval-diff --baseline s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{baseline_id} --candidate s3://.../{run_id}`.
5. If diff points to model quality drop, tag model and trigger rollback policy (automatic if P0 and rollback path configured); otherwise escalate to model team for investigation.

Ownership and escalation matrix
- Applied ML (owner): lead applied-ml@redwood.com -> responsible for eval definitions, prompt-set approvals, quantization recommendations.
- Model Onboarding (owner): model-onboarding@redwood.com -> performance baselines and deployment gating.
- SRE (owner): infra-sre@redwood.com -> CI infra, compute pools, and incident support.
- Product QA (owner): product-qa@redwood.com -> final signoff on quality thresholds for user-facing features.

Postmortem and regression closure criteria
- Create a postmortem for any P0/P1 regression that results in rollback or user-visible degradation. Postmortem must include: timeline, root cause, mitigation steps, and remediation owners.
- Regression is considered resolved when: patch/rollback deployed AND eval-harness daily runs show metrics restored to within 0.5pp of baseline for 3 consecutive runs.

Operational playbook snippets
- Reproduce a failing run locally:
  1. Fetch artifacts: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{run_id}/ ./artifacts --recursive`
  2. Run harness reproduce: `eval-harness-cli reproduce --input ./artifacts/input.jsonl --model {model_uri} --config ./artifacts/config.json --output ./local-repro/ --debug`

- Run quantization quick-check (20% sampling):
  `eval-harness-cli run --prompt-set prompt-set-{id}.jsonl --model {quantized_model_uri} --profile smoke --sample 0.2 --output ./quant-check/`

Governance and periodic reviews
- Quarterly review: Applied ML and Model Onboarding must run a cross-team review of all active prompt-sets, quantization profiles, and baseline models.
- Labels and catalog hygiene: owners must reconcile prompt-set tags and retire sets not used in the last 12 months.

Frequently asked questions
Q: When should a quantized profile be promoted to production?
A: When it is in risk_bucket low or minimal, passes full eval-harness across critical prompt-sets with quality_delta <= 1%, and has a documented rollback plan.

Q: What to do when an infra kernel update causes metric drops?
A: Pin kernel version for affected workload, open infra change ticket referencing SLO breach, and schedule controlled rollout after verification.
